questions.scenario: You are playing a murder mystery board game with your friends. What is your winning strategy?

options.text: Carefully reading the text on the clue cards to find a tiny detail everyone else completely missed.
Looking at the map of the mansion and figuring out who could have moved where without being seen.
Organizing all the suspect cards into categories and running through a logical checklist of elimination.
Focusing on the invisible clues in the story, like trace amounts of a rare poison.

questions.scenario: A gadget at home (like a controller or toaster) stops working. What is your first move?

options.text: I open it completely apart to inspect every single wire and internal gear for damage.
I shine a bright torch through the cracks to see if anything is jammed inside before opening it.
I use testing tools or plug it into different sockets to systematically check the circuits.
I clean out all the dust, lint, and hidden grime that is probably suffocating the sensors.

questions.scenario: When playing a strategy or adventure video game, what is your favorite role or ability?

options.text: The investigator who scans enemies for their specific weaknesses and secret stats.
The scout who uses radar and vision abilities to reveal the map through walls.
The engineer who builds complex traps, manages the inventory, and upgrades the gear.
The alchemist who uses biological attacks, toxic damage, or healing potions.

questions.scenario: Your friend says they are feeling really sick. What is your immediate reaction?

options.text: Asking them to describe the exact type of pain—is it sharp? Does it move? What color is their throat?
Asking if they hit their head or twisted something, checking if anything looks swollen.
Immediately grabbing a smartwatch or thermometer to check their exact temperature and heart rate.
Asking who they were hanging out with recently and figuring out if they caught a virus from someone.

questions.scenario: In art or drawing class, what kind of style do you naturally prefer?

options.text: Highly detailed, close-up sketches with complex, tiny patterns.
3D drawings with intense contrasts between dark shadows and bright highlights.
Technical drawings using rulers and compasses for perfect geometric symmetry.
Abstract, organic shapes that look like growing vines or fluid life forms.

questions.scenario: What annoys you the most when working on a group project?

options.text: When people jump to conclusions without looking at the solid evidence first.
When people lack a 'big picture' vision and get stuck arguing over one tiny thing.
When people are messy, break the rules, and don't follow the correct step-by-step procedure.
When people are unhygienic, like coughing without covering their mouth over the workspace.

questions.scenario: Which of these science experiments sounds the coolest to you?

options.text: Looking at a slice of onion skin or cheek cells under a high-power microscope.
Using magnets or sound waves to visualize things hidden inside a closed box.
Mixing exact amounts of colorful chemicals to create a specific, timed reaction.
Swabbing your phone and growing the bacteria in a petri dish to see what's living on it.

questions.scenario: If you could have one science-fiction superpower, what would it be?

options.text: Microscopic vision, allowing you to see the cells and DNA of any living thing.
X-ray vision, allowing you to see completely through walls and solid objects.
Technopathy, the ability to instantly understand and control any complex machine.
Bio-control, the ability to command microscopic life like bacteria and viruses.

questions.scenario: You are packing for a camping trip in the forest. What safety item is a must-have for you?

options.text: A magnifying glass and tweezers for removing splinters or identifying weird bug bites.
A heavy-duty flashlight to scan dark areas and see what's hiding ahead in the shadows.
A fully stocked, perfectly organized, professional-grade medical kit.
Three different types of hand sanitizers, wet wipes, and water purifiers.

questions.scenario: What kind of YouTube video are you most likely watching at 1 AM?

options.text: A video showing what everyday objects (like a strawberry) look like under a 1000x microscope.
An explanation of how ultrasound machines see babies inside the womb or how X-rays work.
A satisfying compilation of precise factory machines or complex chemistry labs in action.
An epic documentary on how the human immune system battles a virus in a microscopic war.

Pathologist.title: Pathologist / Disease Detective
Pathologist.primary_match_text: You are the ultimate medical detective. You love finding the tiny clues that everyone else misses and relying on cold, hard evidence.
Pathologist.day_in_the_life: Examining tissue samples under a microscope, finding cancer cells, and solving medical mysteries by telling surgeons exactly what disease a patient has.
Pathologist.alternative_match_text: Because you are so highly observant and evidence-based, analyzing cellular data in forensic science or medical research is also a great fit.
Pathologist.roadmap: Take Science (PCB) in 11th/12th. Pursue MBBS (5.5 years), followed by an MD in Pathology (3 years).

Radiologist.title: Radiologist / Imaging Expert
Radiologist.primary_match_text: You are highly visual and tech-savvy. You prefer looking at the 'big picture' and using advanced technology to see what is hidden in the dark.
Radiologist.day_in_the_life: Sitting in a dark, high-tech room analyzing X-rays, MRIs, and CT scans to find broken bones, tumors, or internal bleeding that can't be seen from the outside.
Radiologist.alternative_match_text: Since you have a strong visual-spatial mind and love tech, medical imaging technology or non-invasive diagnostics is your perfect backup path.
Radiologist.roadmap: Take Science (PCB) in 11th/12th. Pursue MBBS (5.5 years), followed by an MD or DNB in Radiodiagnosis (3 years).

Lab_Technologist.title: Medical Laboratory Technologist
Lab_Technologist.primary_match_text: You are hands-on, precise, and highly organized. You love working with machines, following exact procedures, and getting accurate results.
Lab_Technologist.day_in_the_life: Drawing blood, operating million-dollar robotic lab analyzers, and running the crucial chemical tests that doctors rely on to treat patients.
Lab_Technologist.alternative_match_text: With your practical skills and love for precision, operating advanced medical machinery or working in chemical quality control is a highly secure career.
Lab_Technologist.roadmap: Take Science (PCB or PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc in Medical Laboratory Technology (BMLT), followed by specialized certifications.

Microbiologist.title: Clinical Microbiologist
Microbiologist.primary_match_text: You are fascinated by the invisible world. You have a deep curiosity about how tiny things can have massive impacts, and you value hygiene and prevention.
Microbiologist.day_in_the_life: Growing bacteria in petri dishes, hunting down the exact virus causing an outbreak in a hospital, and figuring out which antibiotics will save a patient's life.
Microbiologist.alternative_match_text: Because you are fascinated by microscopic ecosystems, diving into genetics, immunology, or epidemiology (studying outbreaks) is an exciting alternative.
Microbiologist.roadmap: Take Science (PCB) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc in Microbiology or Life Sciences, followed by an M.Sc/PhD in Clinical Microbiology. (Alternatively, MBBS -> MD Microbiology).
